text:
maria: Heads-up RFC follow-up: we need to nail the authz boundaries for org-level API keys vs project-scoped service tokens. Running into routing/visibility issues across Dedicated/Private deployments. Thoughts?
keith: tl;dr: prefer shortest scope by default (project), but allow org keys for cross-project infra ops.
anjali: +1 to project-by-default. main question: how do we route requests that need cross-project model access without leaking permissions?
dave: we could add a broker/exchange flow: org-key -> mint ephemeral project token with scoped perms. No long-lived elevation.
maria: example: analytics job wants embeddings for project A and B in one run. We either give analytics job two tokens or a single org token that can be audited. Which UX wins?
keith: two tokens is safer but awful UX. Broker maybe best: mint ephemeral aggregated token with TTL and auditable parent.
anjali: agree but ops wants simple routing rules in the control plane so Dedicated nodes don't accept org tokens unless allowlist. Security policy: default reject.
dave: ok, propose this rule: Dedicated/Private nodes accept: 1) project-scoped tokens for direct calls; 2) ephemeral tokens minted via control-plane broker that include parent_org_id and ttl; 3) admin org keys only if node config explicitly enables org-scope-mode.
maria: sounds good. How do we represent ephemeral token claims? Need fields for origin, allowed_projects, allowed_models, ttl, issued_by.
keith: sample JWT claims we discussed earlier: 
```
{
  "sub": "svc-analytics",
  "iss": "auth-broker",
  "parent_org": "org-234",
  "allowed_projects": ["proj-A","proj-B"],
  "allowed_models": ["redwood/fast-7b"],
  "exp": 1690000000
}
```
anjali: + add a claim "aud": "redwood-inference-runtime" and a "rotation_id" to tie back to rotation policy.
svc-bot: notice: broker-issued tokens log will contain parent_org and rotation_id for audit. (auto) :white_check_mark:
dave: rollout plan idea: 1) implement broker and token schema; 2) enforce as opt-in on Dedicated; 3) telemetry to capture org-key usage; 4) after 60 days default to deny org-keys on new clusters.
maria: migration concern: we have lots of legacy service keys with wildcard project scope. Need a strategy to remediate without breaking customers.
keith: we should provide an automated migration tool that scans usage and suggests minimal allowed_projects and transforms legacy key -> ephemeral broker flow. Customer approval step required.
anjali: +1, but also require proof: sample prompt set hits and model access mapping. We can auto-generate policy suggestions.
dave: ops question: what about cross-region fallbacks? If broker in region A is unreachable, runtime should be able to validate a signed offline token generated by org admin with short ttl? That seems risky.
maria: fallback policy: allow signed offline tokens only for emergency with limited scopes and shorter TTL, MUST be rotated and revoked ASAP. Log and page on use.
keith: also tie these tokens into rate-limits and per-token quotas so abuse is constrained.
anjali: RBAC surface: we need three primary roles: project-reader/writer, project-deployer (can create tokens scoped to project), org-admin (can mint org-level ephemeral tokens but not long-lived service tokens).
dave: and a machine role: runtime-authorizer (the runtime verifies token claims and can call back to control plane for revocation).
maria: interface for runtime verification: lightweight JWT verify + introspect endpoint for dynamic checks. Example flow: runtime validates signature + exp, checks allowed_models claim subset, then calls /introspect if token has rotation_id or if revocation list changed.
keith: add caching TTL for introspect responses to avoid perf hit. Suggest 30s by default with jitter.
anjali: audit requirements: every mint event, every introspect call, and every refused request due to scope mismatch logged to central audit with parent_org, project, model, route.
nathan: (ops-bot) infra note: Dedicated Private clusters with air-gap can't reach control plane. Broker must run as a local-control-plane component in Private mode.
maria: good catch. So we need two broker modes: cloud-broker (hosted) and local-broker (customer-managed) with same token schema and key material. Document key provisioning flow for local-broker.
dave: doc TODOs: 1) token schema RFC, 2) broker API spec, 3) runtime verification semantics (cache TTLs, introspect shape), 4) migration tool UX and safety checks.
keith: timeline: aim for RFC drafts this week, prototype broker next sprint, opt-in pilot with 2 customers and Dedicated envs in 6 weeks.
maria: one more: how do we handle model-specific permissions (eg model training vs inference)? Probably separate claims: allowed_models: inference, allowed_models_training: true/false. Keep it explicit.
anjali: agree. Also enforce that tokens used for inference cannot be reused for training jobs unless explicitly allowed. 
dave: final: I'll draft the token schema and broker API in a repo PR. @keith @anjali please review. If no objections I'll open RFC doc. :memo: 
maria: thanks all. If anyone has customer examples of legacy wildcard keys share them here so we can prioritize migration helpers.
keith: dropping example from internal customer X in DM.
anjali: will share a sample policy mapping spreadsheet tomorrow.
